agents.claude.acceptEditsDescription: Makes file edits in the working folder without asking; still asks before shell commands.
agents.claude.autoDescription: A safety classifier approves low-risk actions itself and only asks about risky ones.
agents.claude.autoMaybe: Claude Code may not offer Auto with {model}. If it doesn't, it runs in Manual (asking before edits and commands), and Hive shows that mode.
agents.claude.autoUnsupported: Claude Code doesn't offer Auto with {model}: it runs in Manual instead (asking before edits and commands), and Hive shows that mode.
agents.claude.bypassDescription: Never asks and allows everything — any edit, command or network call. Use only in disposable environments.
agents.claude.dontAskDescription: Never prompts. Anything not pre-approved is refused instead of asked about.
agents.claude.extensionNote: You have the Claude Code extension for VS Code (or a similar editor). Hive doesn't use it — the extension's built-in copy moves with every extension update and can't be updated on its own. Install the CLI; your extension keeps working as before.
agents.claude.installNote: The installer runs `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex` in PowerShell and installs to `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin`. After installing, sign in with your Claude account (Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise) or an Anthropic Console account. If the CLI is installed somewhere else, set its path in Settings → Claude Code.
agents.claude.manualDescription: Asks before file edits and shell commands unless you have pre-approved them.
agents.claude.modelPlaceholder: Full model ID, e.g. claude-opus-5-5 or claude-opus-4-6[1m]
agents.claude.planDescription: Read-only: explores and proposes a plan, changes nothing until you approve.
agents.claude.safeguardHelp: In its terminal: /feedback reports a false positive, /model switches back, and /config sets whether it switches models by itself when a message is flagged.
agents.claude.signInHelp: Type /login in one of its agents’ terminals (that agent then carries on by itself), or use Help → Agent Setup → Claude Code → Sign in.
agents.codex.approveForMeDescription: An automatic reviewer approves safe actions itself and only asks about ones it thinks are risky.
agents.codex.askDescription: Reads and edits workspace files and runs commands in its sandbox; asks before internet access or edits outside the workspace.
agents.codex.extensionNote: You have the Codex extension for VS Code (or a similar editor). Hive doesn't use it — the extension's built-in copy moves with every extension update. Install the CLI; your extension keeps working as before.
agents.codex.fullAccessDescription: No sandbox and no approvals: edits anything and uses the internet without asking. Use only in disposable environments.
agents.codex.installNote: The installer runs `irm https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.ps1 | iex` in PowerShell and installs to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\OpenAI\Codex`. After installing, sign in with your ChatGPT account (Plus, Pro, Business or Enterprise) or an API key, then set up its Windows sandbox once. If the CLI is installed somewhere else, set its path in Settings → Codex.
agents.codex.readOnlyDescription: Reads workspace files; asks before any edit or internet access.
agents.codex.safeguardHelp: Codex sends a request it flags to another model, or stops the turn. For security work, OpenAI’s Trusted Access for Cyber program lifts that.
agents.codex.signInHelp: Sign in again in Help → Agent Setup → Codex → Sign in (or run codex login in a terminal).
agents.copilot.acceptEditsCliNote: Copilot’s own footer still says Manual Approval: Hive starts it with edits in its folder approved (an allow rule), which Copilot’s label doesn’t show.
agents.copilot.acceptEditsDescription: Edits files in its folder without asking (not where the folder’s path has parentheses: Copilot can’t approve them there); still asks before other commands, other MCP tools, web access and changes outside its folder.
agents.copilot.allowAllDescription: Approves every tool, path and web request without asking, in its folder and outside it.
agents.copilot.askDescription: Reads files and runs harmless commands without asking; asks before edits, other commands, other MCP tools and web access.
agents.copilot.autopilotDescription: Allow all, and it carries on by itself until the task is done (up to 5 continuations) without handing back to you. Once it has run, the session approves every tool, path and web request, also after you switch out of it. Use only where unattended changes are acceptable.
agents.copilot.extensionNote: You have GitHub Copilot in VS Code (or a similar editor). Hive doesn't use the editor's copy — it moves with every extension update. Install the Copilot CLI; your extension keeps working as before.
agents.copilot.installNote: Install the GitHub Copilot CLI with WinGet (`winget install GitHub.Copilot`) or npm (`npm install -g @github/copilot`), then sign in once with `copilot login` in a terminal (or with the GitHub CLI, which Copilot also uses). Copilot Free runs the Auto model only; choosing a model needs a paid plan. If the CLI is installed somewhere else, set its path in Settings → GitHub Copilot.
agents.copilot.modelPlaceholder: Model ID, e.g. claude-sonnet-5.5 or auto
agents.copilot.planDescription: Plans the work and asks before changing anything.
agents.copilot.signInHelp: Sign in again: run copilot login in a terminal (Help → Agent Setup → GitHub Copilot shows how).
agents.dialog.busy: Busy. Choose it once it has finished.
agents.dialog.name: Name
agents.fileLock.askDescription: The edit waits for your approval, like a permission prompt.
agents.fileLock.blockDescription: An agent that tries to edit a file another agent is editing is told to wait or work on something else.
agents.fileLock.offDescription: Agents edit freely. Use with care when several agents share the project folder.
agents.fileLock.warnDescription: The edit goes ahead, and the agent is told another agent is editing the file.

agents.handOver.busy: {who, select, self {{from} is busy, so it continues from the latest handover.} other {{from} is busy, so {other} continues from the latest handover.} none {{from} is busy, so the other agent continues from the latest handover.}}
agents.handOver.intro: Another agent picks up the work from a handover. It can use a different provider: the conversation itself stays with {agent}; the handover carries the goal, what's done and the next steps. Or {agent} carries on itself in a new conversation, which keeps a long one from slowing things down.
agents.handOver.needsTools: This needs Hive's tools in sessions. Turn on "Provide Hive tools to sessions" in Settings → Agent API.
agents.handOver.running: Running: gets the message in its current session.
agents.handOver.selfNote: Its conversation ends here (it stays in the Sessions tab) and a new one continues from the handover.{size, select, none {} other { Its transcript is {size}.}}
agents.handOver.stopped: {who, select, self {{from} isn't running, so a new conversation continues from the latest handover.} other {{from} isn't running, so {other} continues from the latest handover.} none {{from} isn't running, so the other agent continues from the latest handover.}} Resume {from} first to have it write a new one.
agents.handOver.title: Hand over {agent}'s work to…
agents.handOver.writes: {who, select, self {{from} writes it with Hive's handover tool; {from} continues in a new conversation when it's done.} other {{from} writes it with Hive's handover tool; {other} starts when it's done.} none {{from} writes it with Hive's handover tool; the other agent starts when it's done.}}
